suslicke.title: suslicke.com
suslicke.summary: A developer's personal portfolio with a creative terminal-style interface and command-driven navigation.
suslicke.task: The client needed a portfolio that wouldn't get lost among template sites and would immediately convey the developer's level. We discussed the goal — to stand out while staying usable — the target audience, and which projects and skills mattered most to show first. We fixed the scope: the concept, the section structure, and a fast-loading requirement.
suslicke.solution: We designed navigation around a terminal-style command interface and agreed on the look before development began. We built the site on Next.js: command navigation (about, skills, experience, projects, contact) and an interactive hackme challenge. As we built, we showed progress and refined the interaction details.
suslicke.result: The outcome is a distinctive terminal UX that sticks in memory and sets the portfolio apart from typical solutions. Pages load fast, and the structure stays clear even for first-time visitors to a command interface.
suslicke.approach: The main challenge was balance: keep the striking terminal metaphor without scaring off a visitor expecting a familiar site. We added clear hints and fallback navigation so the command interface feels like a game rather than a barrier. We paid separate attention to performance so animations and interactivity wouldn't slow loading.

animeenigma.title: AnimeEnigma
animeenigma.summary: An anime streaming platform for watching anime online with a large content library.
animeenigma.task: The client wanted to launch a streaming service with a large library that wouldn't fall over as the audience grew. Up front we mapped the usage scenarios, the expected load, and the requirements for a comfortable viewing experience. We fixed the area of responsibility and the priority — stability under load and a smooth player.
animeenigma.solution: As part of a team, I helped build the platform on Next.js with PostgreSQL. I owned the viewing interface and behavior under load: we designed the catalog structure, thought through content delivery, and optimized bottlenecks. We regularly tested across devices and scenarios before shipping.
animeenigma.result: The service runs stably under load and serves a large content library smoothly. Playback stays fluid and the catalog stays responsive even under active traffic.
animeenigma.approach: The key decisions concerned catalog stability and playback smoothness as the user count grew. We worked through caching and careful data handling so heavy lists and title pages stayed fast. We tested behavior on slow connections and varied screens so the viewing experience stayed even.

xaid.title: xaid.ai
xaid.summary: An AI-powered HealthTech product that automatically generates ready-to-sign CT reports reviewed by a radiologist.
xaid.task: The client needed a complex web portal and a powerful admin panel to manage reports, users, and the whole clinical workflow. During requirements we mapped the user roles, the report's path from upload to signature, and the constraints around medical data. We fixed the scope of integrations and the team's working scenarios.
xaid.solution: As part of a team, I contributed to the product: a Next.js web portal, a powerful admin panel, DICOM/HL7 integration, and an AI layer that generates reports. We designed the workflows and admin screens around real scenarios, aligned the interfaces, and assembled them iteratively. We checked data correctness and integration behavior at every step.
xaid.result: The outcome is an international product with a powerful admin panel through which the team runs reports and the whole workflow. Reports are generated automatically and reach the radiologist ready for review and signature.
xaid.approach: The most non-trivial parts were the DICOM/HL7 medical-standard integrations and shaping admin scenarios around sensitive data. We carefully designed the report path and access rights so the process stayed transparent and controllable. We embedded the AI layer so the final decision always rested with the doctor, and the interface helped rather than hindered.
xaid.technologies: Web portal, AI, Admin panel, DICOM/HL7

python-guide.title: Python Guide
python-guide.summary: An educational resource for Python job-interview prep: questions and topics.
python-guide.task: The client needed a handy Python interview-prep reference that ranks well in search. We discussed the audience — candidates at different levels — and how topic navigation should be structured. We set the priority on content structure and technical SEO.
python-guide.solution: We designed the material structure around interview topics and agreed on the presentation before filling it in. We built the site on Next.js and MDX with thoughtful markup, clean URLs, and technical SEO. As content grew, we checked indexing and metadata correctness.
python-guide.result: The resource shows growing organic traffic and stable search rankings. The material is convenient to use while preparing, and the structure expands easily with new topics.
python-guide.approach: The key parts were organizing a large volume of learning material and the technical SEO that search visibility depends on. We thought through the topic structure and the links between topics so users could move through the reference easily. We tuned markup and metadata so pages indexed correctly and looked good in results.

web-interview.title: Web Interview
web-interview.summary: web.drill — an interview-prep platform for web developers with a regularly growing question base.
web-interview.task: The client wanted an interactive interview-prep platform for web developers that's easy to work through and to expand. We mapped the run-through scenarios, the question format, and how to track progress. We fixed the requirement that the base be simple to extend.
web-interview.solution: We built a React interface with a question system, progress tracking, and easy navigation. We designed the structure so the question base would be easy to extend, and aligned the interface behavior before assembly. We checked the run-through experience across devices.
web-interview.result: The platform shows high engagement and maintains a regularly growing question base. Preparation feels comfortable, and adding new questions requires no rework.
web-interview.approach: The main thing was making the run-through engaging while keeping it simple to maintain. We designed the question and progress system so users see forward movement and the team can add new material easily. We separately worked on navigation so returning to topics stays convenient.

loyrush.title: LoyRush
loyrush.summary: A loyalty and gamification SaaS: points, badges, leaderboards and challenges on a subscription model.
loyrush.task: The client needed a loyalty SaaS that retains clients through gamification and gives them clear analytics. Up front we mapped the engagement mechanics, the subscription model, and which metrics matter to clients. We fixed the dashboard scope and the set of game mechanics.
loyrush.solution: We built the frontend on Vue: loyalty mechanics — points, badges, leaderboards, challenges — a subscription model, and a dashboard with analytics. We designed the screens around real client scenarios and aligned the design before development. We assembled the interface iteratively, regularly showing progress.
loyrush.result: The outcome is a working product with a subscription model and clear analytics for clients. Gamification gives users tangible engagement and owners a clear picture of what's happening. The app is also published on the App Store and Google Play.
loyrush.approach: The most substantial part was shaping the game mechanics and the subscription dashboard to be both engaging and clear. We balanced points, badges, and challenges so engagement didn't turn into overload. We designed the dashboard around key metrics so clients see the payoff right away.

exchange-bridge.title: Exchange Bridge
exchange-bridge.summary: A fintech comparison service for international money transfers: compare options and save.
exchange-bridge.task: The client wanted to let users quickly compare ways to send money abroad and pick the cheapest one. We mapped which transfer channels mattered, how to compute the real cost including hidden fees, and how to present the comparison clearly. We fixed the data scope and the requirements for rate freshness.
exchange-bridge.solution: We built a comparison service across transfer options — P2P crypto, banks, Wise, Revolut — with real-time rates (150+ currency pairs, refreshed roughly every 30 seconds), hidden-fee detection, risk scoring, and a live comparison dashboard. We designed the comparison logic and interface so the best option reads at a glance. We checked the accuracy of calculations and the behavior on rate updates.
exchange-bridge.result: The service delivers transparent real-time comparison and helps people save on international transfers. Users see the honest cost of each option with no hidden fees.
exchange-bridge.approach: The most demanding parts were aggregating rates in real time and presenting the comparison clearly. We handled data refresh across many currency pairs carefully so the numbers stayed current and consistent. We built the UX around a single task — quickly seeing the best option, factoring in hidden fees and risk.

ai-diagnostic.title: AI Diagnostic
ai-diagnostic.summary: An AI medical-imaging assistant for radiologists that helps detect pathologies on CT and MRI.
ai-diagnostic.task: The client needed a tool for radiologists that fits into existing infrastructure without rolling out a new system. Up front we mapped how the doctor's workflow is structured and how to connect to PACS with no software install. We set the priority on seamless integration and convenience for the radiologist.
ai-diagnostic.solution: As part of a team, I contributed to the assistant: PACS integration with no software install, pathology detection on CT/MRI, and a convenient interface for radiologists. We designed the interaction so the assistant complements the usual process rather than breaking it. We checked the integration and the way results are presented against real scenarios.
ai-diagnostic.result: The solution is deployed in Russia and takes part in the Moscow Department of Health's computer-vision experiment. The assistant fits into existing infrastructure and helps the doctor within their usual workflow.
ai-diagnostic.approach: The main task was seamless PACS integration with no software install and careful presentation of detection results. We worked out how the assistant fits into the radiologist's usual path so it saves time rather than adding steps. We framed the AI's results as a hint, leaving the final decision with the doctor.

nda-furniture.title: Furniture shop (under NDA)
nda-furniture.summary: An online store selling home furniture. Project details under NDA.
nda-furniture.task: The client needed a convenient online store for selling home furniture. We discussed the general goals and the purchase scenarios and fixed the scope of work. Project details are under NDA.
nda-furniture.solution: As lead developer I owned the whole store: catalog, product pages, cart, and checkout. We ran the work through the standard online-store stages — from design to launch. The specific implementation details aren't disclosed under NDA.
nda-furniture.result: The outcome is a working online store. Its name and details are under NDA.
nda-furniture.approach: This is an online store with the standard e-commerce set: catalog, cart, checkout. The specific decisions and project details aren't disclosed under the non-disclosure agreement.

scioffice.title: SciOffice
scioffice.summary: A no-code/low-code builder for business systems: company, sales, and a marketplace of ready-made apps on a single platform.
scioffice.task: The team needed to bring the product to users from two sides at once: the internal system where the platform itself is assembled and runs, and a clear public landing page that explains the value of the builder and brings in leads. We worked through the audience — businesses, managers, startups, and integrators — the workflows inside the system, and how to present the product on the outside. We fixed the scope of responsibility and priorities.
scioffice.solution: As part of the team I worked on both the platform's internal system and the public landing page. On the system side — the working scenarios of the business-app builder (objects, fields and logic, roles and access); on the landing side — a structure built around a clear pitch and lead capture. We agreed on the interfaces before building and assembled them iteratively, keeping the team in the loop on progress.
scioffice.result: The outcome is a pairing of a working internal system and a public landing page that explains the builder and guides the user toward getting started. The product is presented clearly both outside and inside — from the first impression to real work in the system.
scioffice.approach: The most substantial part was holding two layers within one product: the flexibility of the builder's internal system and the clarity of the public landing page. Inside, we worked through scenarios with objects, fields, logic, and roles so the platform stayed understandable to a non-developer. Outside, we built the landing structure around the product's value so a visitor quickly grasps what it solves and for whom.
scioffice.technologies: No-Code, Low-Code, Business systems, Landing page

nda-school.title: Educational institution portal (under NDA)
nda-school.summary: A portal for an educational institution: class schedule and attendance analytics with a backend, charts, and counters. Name and details under NDA.
nda-school.task: The client needed a portal that brings the class schedule and attendance analytics together in one place and helps see the picture by groups and subjects. We worked through user roles, the schedule workflows, and which metrics matter to track. We fixed the scope of work and the role-based access requirements. Name and details are under NDA.
nda-school.solution: As a developer I owned the backend and the analytics part: class schedule, attendance tracking, charts and counters on dashboards. We added document workflow, role-based access, and background tasks for heavy operations — recomputing analytics, generating reports, and scheduled data rebuilds. Attendance counters and summaries were surfaced so the metrics update without manual work.
nda-school.result: The outcome is a portal where the schedule and attendance live together, and analytics is presented clearly — through charts, counters, and summaries. Heavy operations are moved to the background, so the interface stays responsive. Name and details are under NDA.
nda-school.approach: The most substantial parts were the analytics and the background processing: recomputing attendance, generating reports, and scheduled tasks were moved out of the user's request into a background job queue so the dashboards stay fast. Document workflow and role-based access were built around the institution's real scenarios. Charts and counters were designed so key metrics read at a glance. Details are under NDA.

admp.title: admp.pro
admp.summary: A Telegram bot for automating and running marketplace advertising on Ozon and Wildberries more efficiently.
admp.task: Simplify and speed up managing ad campaigns on Ozon and Wildberries by removing manual routine.
admp.solution: Built a Telegram bot that automates marketplace advertising: campaign management and quick actions right from the messenger.
admp.result: Less manual work and faster reaction to ad changes. Convenient control straight from Telegram.
admp.approach: The key was turning routine Ozon and Wildberries ad actions into simple bot commands. We designed the flows so an operator manages campaigns quickly without extra steps, while the bot handles the repetitive operations.

cost.question: How much does it cost to build a site or app?
cost.answer: The price depends on the task and scope. After a short brief we lock the price and timeline before we start — no hidden add-ons. Landing pages cost less, complex web apps more.

time.question: How long does development take?
time.answer: A landing page — from a few days to a couple of weeks. A web app or SaaS — from several weeks. We give exact timelines after analyzing the task and lock them in our agreement.

support.question: What happens after launch?
support.answer: We stay in touch after launch. Basic support — we keep the site running reliably and available, plus minor fixes. Updates and growth — new features, redesigns, scaling — are a separate paid service. We can take the project on for ongoing maintenance or hand over everything you need to run it yourself.

tech.question: What technologies do you work with?
tech.answer: A modern stack chosen for the task — we pick technology to fit the product, not the other way around, so it stays fast and scalable. Web: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind. Backend: Python, Golang. Mobile: Flutter, React Native. AI and automation: AI/LLM integrations, n8n and building pipelines of AI agents. Not just websites — we build process automation and AI-agent pipelines.

rights.question: Who owns the rights to the code and design?
rights.answer: Everything we build for your project belongs to you — on completion you get full access to the code and assets with no lock-in to us. By default we leave a small, unobtrusive credit in the footer, but we'll remove it if you'd like.

remote.question: Do you work remotely?
remote.answer: We work remotely with clients worldwide. We're based in Kazakhstan and deliver projects across the CIS and abroad — for example, Exchange Bridge and xaid.ai are international products. We communicate via messengers and online meetings — wherever is convenient for you. And if you're in Kazakhstan, especially in Almaty, we can meet in person to discuss the task and lock down the key points at the meeting — which builds trust and speeds up the start.
